name: Wine Jelly
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: 1 pint of wine—pale Sherry or White
ingredients.originalText: 1 pint of wine—pale Sherry or White
ingredients.quantityText: 1 pint of wine—pale Sherry or White

ingredients.name: Juice of two lemons and grated peel of one
ingredients.originalText: Juice of two lemons and grated peel of one

instructions.text: Soak the gelatine in the cold water one hour
Add to this the sugar, lemons, and cinnamon
Pour over all a quart of boiling water, and stir until the gelatine is thoroughly dissolved
Put in the wine, strain through a double flannel bag, without squeezing
Wet your moulds with cold water, and set the jelly away in them to cool

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Soak the gelatine in the cold water one hour
2. Add to this the sugar, lemons, and cinnamon
3. Pour over all a quart of boiling water, and stir until the gelatine is thoroughly dissolved
4. Put in the wine, strain through a double flannel bag, without squeezing
5. Wet your moulds with cold water, and set the jelly away in them to cool
